chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Hammad Abu Yusuf al-Kazzaz from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When there is an heir who has a fixed share (fard), he is more entitled to the property.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Who has priority in inheriting property when there is an heir with a fixed share?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on kinship priority, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of inheritance by affirming that an heir with a fixed statutory share (fard) holds precedence over others. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the sanctity of divinely ordained portions, ensuring that those with explicit Quranic entitlements are satisfied before residual distribution occurs. It serves as a foundational rule for resolving conflicts between heirs with fixed shares and those claiming residual or equal portions.
